cloud.failure_mode: Onboarding (Wi-Fi provisioning) needs the Philips app and account. The local CoAP path documented here works without the cloud on firmware that still exposes it.
cloud.notes: The cloud is the official control route and the one Philips's own app uses; local CoAP is unofficial and some firmware no longer offers it.
cloud.vendor_service: Philips Air+ / Clean Home+ cloud (Versuni), AWS IoT based per the WifiVersion strings

child_lock_off.description: Classic key set: unlock the buttons.

child_lock_on.description: Classic key set: lock the buttons (cl is a JSON boolean).

compact_child_lock_off.description: Compact key set: unlock the buttons (D03103 = 0).

compact_child_lock_on.description: Compact key set: lock the buttons (D03103 = 1).

compact_set_mode.description: Compact key set, models that set mode with D0310C alone (the integration's AC22xx/AC32xx/AC42xx, AC0850 Combo and HU classes): mode code, sent with power on. Codes are model-specific (protocol_details.key_sets.compact-keys.writable.D0310C); the enum is their union. Not for AC0950/AC0951 or AC3420/AC3421, which need compact_set_mode_pair.

mode.description: 0 auto, 1-5 manual speeds (AC22xx/AC32xx/AC42xx), 17 sleep, 18 turbo, 19 medium, 65 high (HU models).

compact_set_mode_pair.description: Compact key set, AC0950/AC0951 and AC3420/AC3421: mode code D0310C and its companion D0310D in one write, as the integration's tables send them. AC0950: auto 0+1, sleep 17+1, medium 19+2, turbo 18+18. AC3420: auto 0+3, sleep 17+1, medium 19+3, turbo 18+18, speeds 1-4 as n+n, speed 5 as 5+18. Send only a listed pair.

companion.description: D0310D, the per-model companion value listed in this command's description.

compact_set_target_humidity.description: Compact key set, humidifying models: target humidity (D03128).

humidity.description: 2-in-1 purifiers (AC3420, AC3421) take 40-70 in steps of 10; HU humidifiers 30-70 in steps of 5. Round to the model's step before sending.

code.description: 0 off, 1 = 30 min, 2-13 = 1-12 h. Some models (the integration's TIMER2 map) do not offer 1.

dashed_power_on.description: Dashed key set (AC1715, AC0850 non-Combo): switch on.

dashed_set_mode.description: Dashed key set: mode by name (D03-12), sent with power on as the integration does.

mode.description: AC1715 offers all five; AC0850 Auto General, Turbo and Sleep.

get_status.description: Read the status (payload_formats.StatusDocument), enveloped. Send with Observe = 0 to subscribe; each notification is a full status.

set_button_light.description: Classic key set: button / UI lights on or off (uil).

set_fan_speed.description: Classic key set: manual fan speed. Most models need mode M in the same or an earlier write (AC2889 per py-air-control; the integration always sends mode with om). Silent is not a mode-M speed: use set_silent.

speed.description: 1-3 speeds, t turbo. (py-air-control also lists s silent, which the integration's AC2729 table sends with mode S, and a for auto, which is mode P; neither goes with mode M.)

set_function.description: Classic key set, 2-in-1 models: purification only or purification plus humidification (func).

function.description: P purification, PH purification and humidification.

set_light_brightness.description: Classic key set: air-quality ring / display brightness (aqil).

brightness.description: Brightness steps py-air-control offers; 0 is off.

set_mode.description: Classic key set: operating mode. Values a given model accepts differ; see protocol_details.key_sets.classic-keys.writable.mode.

mode.description: P auto, A allergen, S sleep, M manual, B bacteria, N night, T turbo, GT gentle; AG and F are accepted by py-air-control without a documented meaning.

set_preferred_index.description: Classic key set: which reading the display shows (ddp).

index.description: 0 IAI, 1 PM2.5, 2 gas, 3 humidity (offered values depend on the sensors fitted).

set_silent.description: Classic key set: silent / night speed. The integration's AC2729 table sends mode S with om s, not mode M.

set_target_humidity.description: Classic key set, humidifying models: target relative humidity (rhset).

humidity.description: The four steps py-air-control and the integration allow (70 is shown as max on the unit).

hours.description: Hours until standby; 0 cancels. dtrs in the status counts down in minutes.

sync.description: Start (or restart) a session: POST eight random uppercase hex digits; the reply (payload_formats.SyncReply) is the counter to continue from. Not enveloped.

nonce.description: 4 random bytes as 8 uppercase hex digits, chosen fresh by the client for each sync (no schema auto kind for random). The device does not echo it.

discovery.none: The encrypted-CoAP units advertise nothing a client can browse for: no mDNS service, and no SSDP answer that the clients use (py-air-control refuses to autodetect for CoAP). A client either takes the address from the user or watches DHCP for the MAC prefixes / "mxchip" hostname in device.identification, as the Home Assistant integration does, then confirms with a sync. A DHCP reservation is recommended; the integration's README says a moved address must be re-entered unless DHCP discovery finds it again. Key a stored unit by the status's DeviceId (32 hex characters), not by its address.

mac_prefixes.notes: DHCP matcher in kongo09/philips-airpurifier-coap manifest.json. Not exclusive to Philips purifiers; ranking only.

identification.notes: The encrypted-CoAP units advertise no mDNS service and answer no SSDP search that the clients rely on (py-air-control refuses to autodetect for CoAP). The Home Assistant integration finds them from DHCP leases: the MAC prefixes above, or a DHCP hostname beginning "mxchip" (the Wi-Fi module vendor), then confirms by completing a sync and reading the status. The decisive identification is therefore a successful POST /sys/dev/sync answered with eight hex digits, followed by a status whose model-id key (modelid, D01-05 or D01S05) names a known model.

device.name: Philips Wi-Fi Air Purifiers and Humidifiers (encrypted CoAP)
device.notes:
Philips connected air purifiers, purifier/humidifier 2-in-1s, standalone humidifiers, fan heaters and fans (model prefixes AC, AMF, CX, HU) expose a small CoAP (RFC 7252) server on UDP 5683 of the home LAN. No vendor account, cloud call or pairing is needed to use it: any host on the LAN can open a session. Three resources carry everything: POST /sys/dev/sync exchanges a 4-byte counter, GET /sys/dev/status with the Observe option streams the device state, and POST /sys/dev/control writes desired state. Status and control payloads are JSON wrapped in an envelope: an 8-hex-digit counter, the AES-128-CBC ciphertext as uppercase hex, and a SHA-256 digest as uppercase hex. The AES key and IV are derived from the counter and a fixed shared string published in every open-source client (protocol_details.envelope), so the encryption authenticates nothing; it only obscures.
GENERATIONS. Philips has shipped three local protocols. (1) The oldest Wi-Fi units (for example AC2729 and AC2889 on early firmware, per py-air-control's README) speak HTTP on port 80 under /di/v1/products/... with a Diffie-Hellman key exchange and AES, are found by SSDP, and take Wi-Fi credentials over that HTTP API. (2) Some units speak plain, unencrypted CoAP on 5683 after an ICMP "hello" (py-air-control's plain_coap client). (3) The encrypted-CoAP generation documented here, which covers every model the Home Assistant integration supports. Only (3) is in scope; (1) and (2) are named so a client can recognise them and are in remaining_unknowns.
KEY SETS. Inside the encrypted-CoAP generation the JSON status keys come in three dialects, chosen by model and Wi-Fi firmware, not by protocol: "classic" short names (pwr, mode, om, pm25, ...), a dashed numeric set (D03-02, D03-12, ...), and a compact numeric set (D03102, D0310C, ...). The three are device.variants here, identified by which model-id key the status carries. Value types differ between them as well (strings, upper-case words, integers) and the compact set requires JSON integers.
LOCAL ACCESS IS FRAGILE. The integration's README warns that some models have newer firmware that no longer allows local connections, and that even working units drop the CoAP session and need a power cycle. Philips's current app ("Air+", and the "Clean Home+" app for newer lines) uses the vendor cloud, not this path. See cloud and remaining_unknowns.

openness.notes: Philips publishes no local API. The encrypted-CoAP envelope was reverse engineered by Radoslav Gerganov (py-air-control, blog post "Controlling the air purifier", xakcop.com) and re-implemented by aioairctrl; the per-model key tables have been crowd-sourced through the kongo09 Home Assistant integration's issue tracker. The shared key-derivation string is a published constant of those projects.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The 3-second Wi-Fi pairing hold in setup is onboarding for the Philips app. A local client never needs it.

exclusivity.recovery: When a unit that used to answer stops answering, power-cycle the purifier. If that is not enough, restart the client as well, which is the Home Assistant integration's own advice for these unstable CoAP stacks. Whether a second client's sync or observation displaces the first has not been established.

pairing.notes: Nothing is asked of a client. POST /sys/dev/sync gives it a counter, and the AES key and IV are derived from that counter plus the fixed string every open-source client publishes (protocol_details.envelope). The SHA-256 trailer is an unkeyed hash. The envelope therefore looks like a session key but authenticates no one: any host on the LAN can read and control the unit, with no account, token or button. The Philips account matters only for onboarding, so the vendor cloud going away would not touch this path. Firmware is what can close it: kongo09/philips-airpurifier-coap warns that newer firmware on some models no longer allows local connections. Sources: py-air-control, aioairctrl and that integration; nothing replayed here.

credentials.notes: The local CoAP path issues nothing: no key, token or session id outlives the sync counter, and the encryption key is derived from public data. Any host on the LAN can read and control the unit. Use `<device-id>` placeholders in notes; a DeviceId is a cloud identifier.
stored_on_device: Cloud identity (DeviceId, ProductId) used by the Philips app

factory_reset.description: Philips's support page gives one general procedure without naming models. It is separate from the Wi-Fi pairing-mode hold (which only re-pairs) and from the filter-counter reset (the AC0850/20 manual: hold the mode button for 5 seconds), neither of which is a factory reset.
factory_reset.effect: Philips support describes this as the reset needed when the unit was previously bound to a different Philips account; what else it clears (Wi-Fi credentials, filter counters, settings) is not stated.

procedures.basis: Philips support article XC000019027, 'I cannot connect my Philips Air Purifier with the App' (general, not model-specific).
procedures.name: Power and mode held together

steps.action: With the unit powered, hold the power button and the mode button together for 10 seconds until it beeps.
Wait for the unit to restart and re-enter Wi-Fi pairing mode, then pair it again with the app.

cloud.local_alternative: None known for this generation. py-air-control can set Wi-Fi locally only on the older HTTP generation (PUT /di/v1/products/0/wifi on the PHILIPS Setup network); no source documents a local provisioning exchange for encrypted-CoAP units.

methods.description: Two steps in order: put the purifier into Wi-Fi pairing mode on the device, then let the Philips app (Air+ for the models in this spec; a Philips account is required) push the home Wi-Fi credentials. The app is needed only for this; local control then works without it while the firmware still allows it.
methods.name: Pair with the Philips app, then talk CoAP locally

stages.description: The button differs by model. The AC0850/20 manual says to power the unit on and then hold a button for 3 seconds until it beeps (the extracted text does not name it; check the model's manual); py-air-control's README says the AC2729 enters pairing mode with power and child-lock held together for 3 seconds. In pairing mode the Wi-Fi indicator blinks orange and the unit opens an open access point named "PHILIPS Setup".
stages.name: Enter Wi-Fi pairing mode

steps.action: Power the unit on, then hold the model's Wi-Fi pairing button (or button pair) for about 3 seconds until it beeps.
steps.expect: The Wi-Fi indicator blinks orange; a network named PHILIPS Setup appears.

cloud.local_alternative: None known for this generation. py-air-control can set Wi-Fi locally only on the older HTTP generation (PUT /di/v1/products/0/wifi on the PHILIPS Setup network); no source documents a local provisioning exchange for encrypted-CoAP units.

stages.description: The app signs in to the Philips account, joins the PHILIPS Setup network and hands over the home network's SSID and passphrase. Philips support requires a 2.4 GHz network and a passphrase of at most 63 characters without special symbols. The provisioning exchange of this generation is not documented by any source read (see remaining_unknowns).
stages.name: Provision Wi-Fi from the Philips app

steps.action: In the Philips app, add a new device and follow its prompts while the unit is in pairing mode.
steps.expect: The Wi-Fi indicator turns solid white once the unit is online.

steps.action: Find the unit's LAN address (router DHCP table) and POST a random 8-hex-digit string to /sys/dev/sync on UDP 5683.
steps.expect: The unit answers with eight hex digits (its counter); local control is available.

setup.notes: Wi-Fi onboarding is done by the Philips app with a Philips account; no open-source client implements it for the encrypted-CoAP generation (py-air-control's Wi-Fi setter works only on the HTTP generation). Once the unit is on the LAN, the local CoAP path needs no credential, token or pairing: setup for a local client is just knowing the address.

rejoin.notes: A changed router means pairing mode (the 3-second hold above) and provisioning from the Philips app again; no local command sets Wi-Fi on this generation. Afterwards the unit has a new address, so a local client must re-learn it.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The envelope (sync, MD5-derived AES-128-CBC key and IV, SHA-256 trailer) is transcribed from three independent open-source clients that agree byte for byte (py-air-control, aioairctrl, and aioairctrl 0.3.1 as used by the Home Assistant integration). scripts/test_philips_air_coap_spec.py rebuilds every example envelope in this file from the stated rule with invented counters. The key tables per model generation come from the Home Assistant integration's model classes, which are built from owner-submitted status dumps.

entities.name: Purifier
entities.notes: Power only. Speed is a mode/om pair whose valid combinations are model-specific, so it is exposed as the Mode and Fan Speed selects rather than as set_percentage. Prefer observing get_status to polling.

entities.name: Mode
entities.notes: Not every model offers every mode (kongo09 philips.py lists them per model).

entities.name: Fan Speed
entities.notes: Selecting a speed also sets mode M. Silent (om s) is left out because it needs mode S; it is commands.set_silent. In auto mode om reports the automatic speed (and may read a); in silent it reads s.

entities.name: Off Timer
entities.notes: 0-12 hours; dtrs gives the minutes left.

entities.name: Water Level
entities.notes: Humidifying models. The integration shows 0 whenever err is 32768 or 49408 (tank open / no water).

entities.name: HEPA Filter Remaining
entities.notes: Hours until replacement. Pre-filter is fltsts0, carbon fltsts2, wick wicksts; flttotal* give the totals on newer firmware.

entities.name: Filter Remaining
entities.notes: NanoProtect filter hours left; D05-08 is the total.

entities.name: Mode
entities.notes: Read-only on purpose. Setting the mode takes compact_set_mode on most compact models but compact_set_mode_pair (with D0310D) on AC0950 and AC3420, and the three key-set variants cannot tell those groups apart, so one select binding would send an incomplete write to some units. Union of the per-model codes.

entities.name: PM2.5
entities.notes: Purifiers only; absent on HU humidifiers and CX heaters.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.notes: Raw value is tenths of a degree.

entities.name: Filter Remaining
entities.notes: NanoProtect filter hours left; D05408 is the total, D0520D/D05207 the pre-filter.

entities.name: Target Humidity
entities.notes: Humidifying models only; 2-in-1 purifiers accept 40-70 in steps of 10.

evidence.documentation_review: Read 2026-11-01: py-air-control master (coap_client.py, airctrl.py, status_transformer.py, http_client.py, plain_coap_client.py, README), aioairctrl master and the 0.3.1 sdist from PyPI (encryption.py, client.py, tests/test_encryption.py), and kongo09/philips-airpurifier-coap master (const.py, philips.py, helpers.py, coordinator.py, manifest.json, README) plus issues #190, #318, #326 and #345. All three clients agree on paths, port, envelope layout, MD5 key/IV split, SHA-256 trailer and the control wrapper. aioairctrl 0.3.1's own test suite decrypts two real device captures (an AC0850/11 dashed-key status and an AC2729/10 classic-key status), which confirms the envelope against devices; those captures are not reproduced here because they carry real device ids.
evidence.open_questions: Which firmware versions removed local access, and on which models; the provisioning exchange on PHILIPS Setup for this generation; whether the device rejects reused or out-of-order counters; what AC0650/AC0651 and AC1715 units that refuse CoAP speak instead.
evidence.status_correction: The backlog note expected an HMAC-SHA-256 trailer. Every client computes a plain SHA-256 over counter + ciphertext hex; no key is involved.

dfu_mode.notes: How the unit behaves while updating is not established.

enter.notes: No local command that starts or blocks an update is documented.

image.notes: Units update themselves over the internet (the status carries otacheck and, on classic firmware, ota keys). Owners report that an update has removed or broken local CoAP access; the integration README warns of it without naming versions. Blocking the unit's internet access is the owners' reported way to keep a working firmware. No local upload path is known.

local_access.summary: Encrypted CoAP on UDP 5683 with a public key-derivation string: no account, token or pairing. Works on the models in protocol_details.key_sets while their firmware still exposes it.

ControlReply.description: Plain JSON body of the reply to POST /sys/dev/control (not enveloped).

fields.description: "success" when the write was accepted; anything else is a failure.
fields.name: status

StatusDocument.description: The decrypted body of every GET /sys/dev/status response and notification. Values here are invented, classic key set; see protocol_details.key_sets for the dashed and compact sets, which use the same wrapper.

fields.description: Object of status keys; which keys appear depends on model and key set.
fields.name: state.reported

parse_rules: Decode the envelope (protocol_details.envelope.decode), then parse JSON.
Choose the key set by which model-id key is present: modelid (classic), D01-05 (dashed), D01S05 (compact).
Treat a missing key as 'not on this model', not as zero; humidity, water and wick keys exist only on humidifying models.

SyncReply.description: Plain-text body of the 2.xx reply to POST /sys/dev/sync.

fields.description: Eight uppercase hex digits: the device's current counter. The next client envelope uses this value plus one.
fields.name: counter

protocol_details.control_document: Every write is one JSON object: {"state": {"desired": {"CommandType": "app", "DeviceId": "", "EnduserId": "", <key>: <value>, ...}}}. The three fixed members are sent empty by every client. Several keys may be set in one write (the integration sends power and mode together). Keys and value types follow the unit's key set (variants); the same write with the wrong set's keys is accepted with "success" by some units and ignored (reported in the integration's issues, not established as a rule).

envelope.cipher: AES-128-CBC, PKCS#7 padding to 16 bytes, over the UTF-8 JSON plaintext.
envelope.decode: counter = first 8 chars; D = last 64; C = the rest. Check D, derive key and IV from counter, decrypt C, strip PKCS#7, parse JSON.
envelope.digest: D = uppercase hex of SHA-256( ASCII(counter + C) ) where C is the uppercase hex ciphertext. A plain hash, not an HMAC: it is keyed by nothing and detects corruption only. Clients reject a device envelope whose D does not match.
envelope.key_derivation: H = uppercase hex of MD5( ASCII(shared_secret + counter) ), where counter is the 8 uppercase hex digits. H is 32 characters. The AES key is the ASCII bytes of H[0:16] and the CBC IV the ASCII bytes of H[16:32] (16 bytes each, so AES-128). The hex characters themselves are the key material; H is NOT hex-decoded.
envelope.layout: counter (8 chars) || C (uppercase hex, 32*n chars) || D (64 chars), one ASCII string, no separators.
envelope.shared_secret_notes: A fixed ASCII string published as a constant in py-air-control (coap_client.py) and aioairctrl (coap/encryption.py). It is the same for every unit; it is not a per-device or per-user key.

test_vectors.name: classic-keys power on, after a sync answered 6D2C0F41
compact-keys power on plus turbo, after a sync answered FFFFFFFE
classic-keys status notification from a device (invented values)

envelope.vector_notes: All counters, names and ids are invented. The control plaintexts use Python json.dumps default spacing because that is byte for byte what py-air-control and aioairctrl send; compact JSON is not known to be rejected but has not been reported either.

classic-keys.identity: modelid (e.g. AC2729/10), type, name, swversion, WifiVersion (e.g. AWS_Philips_AIR@62.1), ProductId, DeviceId, Runtime (ms), rssi (dBm), err.

readable.aqit: Air-quality notification threshold (an app setting, not a sensor).
readable.err: Error bit field; 0 none. Reported values: 193 pre-filter must be cleaned, 49155 pre-filter must be cleaned, 32768 water tank open, 49408 no water. The integration reads bit 8 (0x100) as 'out of water'.
readable.fltsts1: HEPA filter replace-in, hours; fltt1 its type code (e.g. A3).
readable.fltsts2: Active-carbon filter replace-in, hours; fltt2 its type code (e.g. C7).
readable.flttotal0: Pre-filter total life, hours (newer classic firmware; the integration uses it as the 100 % mark when present).
readable.tvoc: Total VOC index (models with a gas sensor).
readable.wl: Water level %, 0 or 100 in captures (humidifier models).

writable.ddp: string preferred index on the display: "0" IAI, "1" PM2.5, "2" gas, "3" humidity.
writable.dt: integer off-timer in hours 0-12 (0 = off); dtrs reports minutes left.
writable.func: string P purification only, PH purification and humidification (2-in-1 models).
writable.mode: string. P auto (purification), A allergen, S sleep, M manual, B bacteria, N night, T turbo, GT gentle, AG and F also accepted by py-air-control; which a model offers varies (philips.py per model).
writable.om: string fan speed: "1" "2" "3", "s" silent, "t" turbo, "a" auto. AC2729 sets speed by mode M plus om, and night by mode S plus om s; py-air-control notes the AC2889 needs mode M and om together.

compact-keys.identity: D01S03 name, D01S05 model id, D01S12 software version, plus WifiVersion, ProductId, DeviceId, Runtime, rssi.
compact-keys.models: AC0850/xx whose WifiVersion begins AWS_Philips_AIR_Combo, AC0850/81, AC0950, AC0951, AC2210, AC2220, AC2221, AC3210, AC3220, AC3221, AC3420, AC3421, AC3737, AC4220, AC4221, AMF765, AMF870, CX3120, CX3550, CX5120, HU1509, HU1510, HU4209, HU4210, HU5710.

readable.D0313F: Heater action: 65 strong, 67 medium, 68 low, -16 idle, 0 fan.
readable.D03240: Error bit field; bit 8 (0x100) out of water, as in the classic set.
readable.D0520D: Pre-filter clean-in, hours; D05207 its total.
readable.D0540E: NanoProtect filter replace-in, hours; D05408 its total.

compact-keys.value_type_rule: Every D03 value is a JSON integer; kongo09 issue #326 (CX3120) reports that strings are not accepted.

writable.D03105: display backlight on other models: 0 off, 115 medium, 123 on, 101 auto (where offered).
writable.D0310A: function on fans/heaters: 1 fan, 2 circulation, 3 heating (CX models). On 2-in-1s, 4 reads as humidification on.
writable.D0310C: mode. AC22xx/AC32xx/AC42xx: 0 auto, 1-5 manual speeds, 17 sleep, 18 turbo, 19 medium. AC0850 Combo: 0 auto, 17 sleep, 18 turbo. AC0950/AC3420 also set D0310D alongside. HU1509/HU1510/HU4209/HU4210/HU5710: 0 auto, 17 sleep, 19 medium, 65 high.
writable.D0310D: fan speed companion to D0310C on some models (AC0950: 1 with auto/sleep, 2 medium, 18 turbo).
writable.D03110: off-timer: 0 off, 1 30 min, 2-13 = 1-12 h (some models lack 1).
writable.D03128: target humidity: 40-70 step 10 (2-in-1s) or 30-70 step 5 (HU models).
writable.D03135: lamp mode: 0 off, 1 air-quality or humidity ring, 2 ambient light.
writable.D03137: ambient light style: 1 warm, 2 dawn, 3 calm, 4 breath.
writable.D0320F: oscillation angle (fans/heaters; 0 off, model-specific on values).

dashed-keys.identity: D01-03 name, D01-05 model id, D01-07 language, D01-21 software version, plus WifiVersion, ProductId, DeviceId, Runtime, rssi.
dashed-keys.models: AC1715 and AC0850/xx whose WifiVersion begins AWS_Philips_AIR (not _Combo), AC0850/85.

readable.D05-13: Pre-filter clean-in, hours; D05-07 its total (e.g. 720).
readable.D05-14: NanoProtect filter replace-in, hours; D05-08 its total (e.g. 4800); D05-02 its type code.

writable.D03-12: string mode: "Auto General", "Gentle/Speed 1", "Speed 2", "Turbo", "Sleep" (AC1715); AC0850 offers Auto General, Turbo, Sleep.

other_generations.http: Older Wi-Fi purifiers: HTTP on port 80, GET/PUT /di/v1/products/1/air (status and control), /di/v1/products/0/wifi (Wi-Fi credentials, settable), /di/v1/products/0/firmware, /di/v1/products/1/fltsts, a Diffie-Hellman exchange on /di/v1/products/0/security yielding an AES session key, and SSDP discovery on UDP 1900 (py-air-control http_client.py). The same classic JSON keys. Not covered by this spec.
other_generations.plain_coap: Some units answer unencrypted JSON on /sys/dev/status and /sys/dev/control after an ICMP and empty-CoAP "hello" (py-air-control plain_coap_client.py). Not covered by this spec.

session.control_reply: POST /sys/dev/control answers a plain (not enveloped) JSON body. Success is exactly {"status":"success"} (py-air-control compares the string); anything else is a failure, after which aioairctrl re-syncs once and retries up to five times.
session.counter: The counter is a 32-bit big-endian value written as exactly 8 uppercase hex digits. Before EVERY envelope it encrypts, the client adds one to its counter and uses the result: the first control write after a sync answered "6D2C0F41" is enveloped under "6D2C0F42". aioairctrl 0.3.1 wraps FFFFFFFF to 00000000; the original aioairctrl raised on overflow and py-air-control dropped leading zeros (it writes the counter without padding), so behaviour at the edges is client-specific and untested on a device. Device envelopes carry the device's own counter, which a client reads from the first 8 characters and does not have to track.
session.observe: GET /sys/dev/status with Observe = 0 registers an observation (RFC 7641); the first response is the full current status and every later notification on the token is a full status again, not a delta. aioairctrl reads Max-Age from the response (60 s if absent) and the Home Assistant integration treats three missed Max-Age periods as a dead session and reconnects (new context, new sync, new observation). A one-shot read is the same GET; the clients simply stop after the first response.
session.sync: POST /sys/dev/sync, NON, body = 8 random uppercase hex digits (4 random bytes). The device answers with 8 hex digits: the counter the client must continue from. The client's random value is not used again by any client. A new sync may be done at any time; the clients re-sync after a failed control write and on reconnect.

protocol_details.transport: CoAP (RFC 7252) over plain UDP, port 5683, URI coap://<host>:5683/<path>. No DTLS. Every client sends NON (non-confirmable) messages. Payloads are ASCII text; the status and control bodies are the envelope below, the sync body and the control reply are not enveloped.

remaining_unknowns: Firmware that removes local access: the integration README says some models have newer firmware that does not allow local connections, and forum owners report the same after automatic updates, but no source names a version or a model list. Issue #345 (AC2220/10 on 0.2.1) turned out to be a network problem, not firmware.

Models that never answered: kongo09 issue #318 says nobody has found a way to talk to the AC0651 (firmware 0.2.1; it pings but ignores CoAP), and #190 reports AC1715/11 units refusing the connection, with the maintainer suggesting some units may not offer encrypted CoAP at all.

Counter rules on the device side: whether it rejects a reused, skipped or out-of-order counter, whether it enforces the SHA-256 trailer on client envelopes, and what a write with a stale counter answers. Clients re-sync on any non-success.
Counter edges: aioairctrl 0.3.1 wraps FFFFFFFF to 00000000 and zero-pads; py-air-control does not pad; device behaviour at either edge is untested.
Wi-Fi provisioning of this generation over the PHILIPS Setup access point is not implemented by any open-source client; only the HTTP generation's /di/v1/products/0/wifi PUT is.

The compact-key mode table is per model: the integration's AC22xx, AC0850 Combo and HU classes send D0310C alone (compact_set_mode), while AC0950 and AC3420 also send D0310D (compact_set_mode_pair). The compact Mode entity is read-only until variants can be told apart by model value (a variant whose identification excludes a model, or a per-model command table); the schema has no such negative match today.

Value types for classic writes are inconsistent between clients: py-air-control sends om, pwr, mode, uil and ddp as strings and rhset, aqil, dt as integers, matching what the status reports; which the firmware strictly requires is unverified.
Wi-Fi passphrase protection during provisioning is unknown.
The HTTP generation (SSDP, Diffie-Hellman, /di/v1) and the plain-CoAP generation are named in protocol_details.other_generations but not specified.

Schema gaps: there is no CoAP transport block (commands use transport coap with method/path and the session rules live in protocol_details, plus a placeholder http_endpoints entry), no declarative envelope or framing scheme for an encrypted CoAP body (hence protocol_handler philips_air_coap), no DHCP discovery method (the MAC/hostname matchers live in identification notes), and no way to say a command's body is a key-set dialect beyond variants.
